member.name: T:ArchiMetrics.CodeReview.Rules.AllRules
member.summary: The entry point to this library: discovers every review rule it contains and hands them to a NodeReviewer.
member.remarks: Rules are found by reflection rather than listed here, so adding a rule is a matter of writing the class and nothing else — there is no registry to forget to update. The individual rule types stay internal for the same reason: callers choose which sets of rules to run, not which concrete classes, which leaves the library free to add, split or rename rules without breaking anyone.

member.name: M:ArchiMetrics.CodeReview.Rules.AllRules.GetSyntaxRules(ArchiMetrics.Analysis.Common.CodeReview.ISpellChecker)
member.summary: Gets every syntax rule in the library — the rules that inspect code shape without needing type information, and so the cheaper of the two sets to run.
member.param: The spell checker handed to rules that examine identifiers and comments for real words. May be , in which case those rules are still created but have nothing to check against — pass one if you want naming and comment-language rules to do anything.
member.returns: The rules, ordered by ID so that results are stable between runs.

member.name: M:ArchiMetrics.CodeReview.Rules.AllRules.GetSymbolRules
member.summary: Gets every symbol rule in the library — the rules that need a resolved semantic model, and so can reason about what a name actually refers to rather than only how the code is written.
member.remarks: These cost more to run than the syntax rules because they require a compilation, which is why the two sets are exposed separately: a caller doing a quick pass can take the syntax rules alone.
member.returns: The rules, one instance of each parameterless type found in the assembly.

member.name: M:ArchiMetrics.CodeReview.Rules.Code.EvaluationBase.GetLinesOfCode(Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: Gets the number of source lines the node occupies, for reporting how much code a violation covers. Blank lines, comments and documentation are excluded.

member.name: M:ArchiMetrics.CodeReview.Rules.Code.EvaluationBase.GetExecutableStatements(Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.SyntaxNode)
member.summary: Gets the number of executable statements in the node.
member.remarks: Size rules test against this rather than against physical lines so that reformatting a method — wrapping a long argument list, splitting a condition over two lines — cannot push it over a limit. A rule that fires on layout rather than on substance teaches developers to fight the tool.

member.name: M:ArchiMetrics.CodeReview.Rules.Code.MissingEventHandlerDetachmentRule.IsLikelyEventSubscription(Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Syntax.AssignmentExpressionSyntax)
member.summary: Determines whether the right-hand side of a += expression is likely a delegate or method group (i.e., an event subscription). Event handlers are assigned as bare method names (SomeEvent += Handler), member accesses (SomeEvent += obj.Handler), lambda expressions, or explicit delegate constructors (new EventHandler(Handler)). Anything else — invocations, literals, arithmetic — is not an event subscription.

member.name: M:ArchiMetrics.CodeReview.Rules.Semantic.ClassInstabilityRule.IsReferencedFromTest(ArchiMetrics.Analysis.ReferenceResolvers.ReferenceLocation)
member.summary: Test code depends on production code by design, so counting it would make a class look more depended-upon - and therefore more stable - than it really is in the shipping application. Only references from non-test code describe the real coupling.

member.name: T:ArchiMetrics.CodeReview.Rules.Semantic.TooLowMaintainabilityIndexRule
member.summary: Flags methods whose maintainability index has fallen far enough that changing them is likely to be slow and error-prone.
member.remarks: The trigger point comes from rather than a literal in this file. Sharing it with the reporting side is what stops the tool from contradicting itself — a summary describing a method as merely "Concerning" while this rule reports the same method as a defect would leave the reader with no idea which to trust.

member.name: M:ArchiMetrics.CodeReview.Rules.Semantic.TooLowMaintainabilityIndexRule.#ctor(System.Int32)
member.summary: Initialises the rule with a custom trigger point, for callers who want to be stricter or more lenient than the library default.
member.param: A maintainability index on the 0-100 scale. Methods at or below it are reported.

member.name: P:ArchiMetrics.CodeReview.Rules.Semantic.TooLowMaintainabilityIndexRule.Threshold
member.summary: Gets the maintainability index at or below which a method is reported. On the 0-100 maintainability scale, where higher is better.
